description: TAYO is an independent team focused on Earth observation, geospatial analysis, environmental science, and interactive data visualization. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to explore landscape changes between Lakes Ranco and Puyehue in southern Chile using NISAR radar data. Our goal is to make satellite observations accessible and useful for understanding forests, ecosystems, and environmental transformations.
summary:
TAYO is an interactive observatory that will help people learn about and better understand places of interest to them. Through an interactive map, users can explore the characteristics of a landscape, access environmental information, and identify differences between satellite observations.

Its first prototype focuses on southern Chile, between Lakes Ranco and Puyehue. It integrates radar observations from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission, precipitation estimates from NASA GPM IMERG, and land cover maps from CONAF.

TAYO addresses the Dancing with the SARs challenge by making complex scientific information more accessible to individuals, communities, students, and professionals. It presents observations alongside their dates, sources, and limitations, without automatically attributing causes to the detected variations. The project is designed to expand to other territories where compatible data is available and, in the future, incorporate additional information such as flora and fauna.
details:
TAYO — Landscape Change Observatory


Know your territory. Explore its transformations. Understand what you're seeing.


Every place has a story worth understanding

A forest can change without us noticing. A river can reshape its surroundings. Rainfall can temporarily transform a landscape. A place we know today may have looked very different in the past.

Sometimes we want to understand what is happening in a particular place, but we don't know where to find reliable information or how to interpret it.

What is the forest near my home like? What information is available about a piece of land I want to learn more about? Have any changes been observed in a particular area of the landscape?

The information exists. What's missing is making it accessible, understandable, and useful to people.


Our proposal: TAYO

TAYO is an interactive observatory designed to help anyone discover and better understand the places that interest them.

The idea is simple: choose a location on the map and explore what we can learn about it.

By bringing together geographic, environmental, and satellite information, TAYO allows users to explore the characteristics of a landscape, observe variations between different dates, and examine conditions that might help explain them.

It is designed for people who are curious about their surroundings, as well as communities, students, and professionals working in environmental sciences, forestry, agriculture, real estate, and land-use planning.


What can you discover?

  • Get to know a place: Explore its geographic characteristics, vegetation, and land cover.
  • Observe variations: Identify differences recorded by satellites between different dates.
  • Understand its context: Explore historical information about the territory and recent precipitation.
  • Dig deeper: Access data, observation dates, sources, and scientific limitations.

TAYO distinguishes between what has been observed and what still requires further investigation. It does not invent diagnoses or automatically turn a satellite signal into a conclusion.


Our starting point

We begin in southern Chile, between Lakes Ranco and Puyehue, using observations from the NISAR mission, precipitation data from NASA GPM IMERG, and historical land-cover maps from CONAF.

This territory is our first area of exploration, but TAYO is designed to expand to any region of the world where compatible data is available.


Our vision

We believe that understanding our planet should not require specialized knowledge or depend on tools that are difficult to use.

We want to transform complex scientific information into clear answers that help people learn about, investigate, and understand the places that matter to them.


Prototype Development and Functionality

TAYO is an interactive web application developed with JavaScript, Vite, and Leaflet. It allows users to explore a territory through maps, select locations or areas of interest, and access geographic, environmental, and satellite information.

The prototype uses radar observations from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission acquired on October 24 and November 5, 2026. It allows users to explore individual observations and experimentally compare differences using HH and HV polarizations.

These observations are complemented by historical land-cover maps from CONAF, precipitation estimates from NASA GPM IMERG, and NASA OPERA products related to vegetation disturbances and the presence of surface water.

The application includes territorial information panels, explanations of the data, geographic selection tools, a glossary, and options to generate reports at different levels of detail. It also allows users to record field observations and maintain local tracking of places of interest.

One of TAYO's fundamental principles is to distinguish between satellite measurements, environmental classifications, and possible interpretations. Therefore, variations in radar observations and experimental layers are not presented as scientifically validated diagnoses or as evidence of specific events.

The project combines different sources to facilitate territorial exploration and provides information about the dates, provenance, and limitations of the data, prioritizing an experience that is understandable to people without specialized technical knowledge.

The prototype demonstrates this experience in southern Chile, between Lakes Ranco and Puyehue, and establishes a technological foundation that can be extended to other territories where compatible data is available.


NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Dancing with the SARs.
